paper_title: Novel cosmological bounds on thermally-produced axion-like particles
notes: Headline result of the paper is the axion-gluon coupling bound from Planck 2018 CMB + BAO (abstract: 'most stringent bounds on the axion-gluon coupling to date ... superseding the current bounds from SN1987A'). Points read from Fig. 8, right axis g_d [GeV^-2], the Planck+BAO blue diamonds (fuller dataset; Planck-only orange diamonds are similar within a factor). 95% CL upper bounds at the 9 fixed masses m_a = {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,0.1,1,3,10,30,100} eV used in the LCDM+DNeff fixed-mass runs. The figure is a raster embedded in the vector PDF; y-axis calibrated using the two green SN1987A horizontal lines at g_d=7.7e-6 (y=202px) and g_d=6.7e-9 (y=542px) from Eq. 5.4, cross-checked against the frame bottom (C_g/f_a=1e-12 -> g_d=3.5e-15). The paper directly constrains the axion-gluon coupling C_g/f_a; g_d is obtained via the model-dependent relation g_d = (C_angamma/m_n)(C_g/f_a) with C_angamma~=0.0033 (Eqs. 2.4/coupling-gd), plotted on the right axis. Marginalised full-range bound (Table 2, Planck+BAO): g_d < 3.77e-10 GeV^-2. This is a cosmological CMB constraint independent of local DM density (dm_density_assumed=null). The paper also gives an axion-photon coupling bound (Fig. 7), but the gluon/EDM coupling is presented as the primary/most novel result.
